question.text: If $U_n(n=1,2)$ denote the $n^{\text {th }}$ derivative $(n=1,2)$ of $U(x)=\frac{L x+M}{x^2-2 B x+C}(L, M, B, C$ are constants $)$, then $P U_2+Q U_1$ $+R U=0$, holds for

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Hint: } U(x)=\frac{L x+m}{x^2-2 B x+c}, U(x)\left(x^2-2 B x+c\right)=L x+m \\ & U(x)(2 x-2 B)+\left(x^2-2 B x+c\right) U_1(x)=L \\ & U(x)2 \times 2(2 x-2 B) U_1(x)+(2 x-2 B) U_1(x)+\left(x^2-2 B x+c\right) U_2(x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow U_2\left(x^2-2 Bx+c\right)+U_1(4 x-4 B)+2 U=0 \\ & \therefore P=x^2-2 B x+c, Q=4(x-B), R=2\end{aligned}$
